# Awesome Video MLLM Architectures

![Awesome Video MLLM Architectures](assets/banner.svg)

An illustrated collection of video multimodal large language models: how frames become visual tokens, how temporal evidence reaches the language decoder, and how long or live video is kept in memory.

**70 illustrated records** · 64 model/version/family cards · 6 method/system cards · reviewed through **2026-10-08**.

Every card includes a local diagram, architecture explanation, temporal mechanism, training or inference recipe, and primary sources. Primary diagrams comprise 65 author figures and 5 explicitly labeled editorial schematics. A family or training recipe can share an existing backbone; record count is not a count of independent architectures.

The organization is inspired by [Awesome VLM Architectures](https://github.com/gokayfem/awesome-vlm-architectures). Descriptions are newly written and figure provenance is recorded. The initial Chinese research is preserved in [RESEARCH.zh-CN.md](RESEARCH.zh-CN.md).

## Model architectures

Cards appear from newest to oldest. Click a diagram to view the original local asset at full size. The expandable section explains the architecture and distinguishes structural changes from data or training contributions.

<a id="21-videochat3"></a>

### VideoChat3

VideoChat3 inflates image-transformer attention into local 3D video attention, combining early spatiotemporal compression with adaptive resolution for offline, long-video, and proactive streaming understanding.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14935) · [Code](https://github.com/MCG-NJU/VideoChat3)

**Authors:** Xinhao Li et al.  
**First public date:** 2026-07-16 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** video encoder, token compression, streaming architecture, instruction data

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/21-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/21-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoChat3: Author figure: architecture overview of VideoChat3." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.14935v2#S2.F2). Author figure: architecture overview of VideoChat3.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** I3D-ViT groups consecutive frames into short chunks and expands pretrained 2D spatial attention into 3D spatiotemporal attention. Spatial 2×2 merging and temporal pooling compress tokens before an MLP projector and language model. For streaming inputs, generated state tokens control frame-resolution quotas, allocating more visual detail around uncertain or important moments before issuing a response.

**Temporal modeling.** Local 3D attention captures motion before compression. Chunk-wise temporal pooling reduces redundancy, while streaming state transitions regulate when additional evidence and higher resolution are needed.

**Training / inference recipe.** Apply four stages: visual-tokenizer pretraining, video-language alignment, general video instruction tuning, and long/streaming instruction tuning. Projector warm-up precedes joint adaptation; the final stage trains the projector and LLM using long-form and response-timing supervision.

**Data mentioned in the source:** VideoChat3-Academic2M, VideoChat3-LV116K, streaming instruction data.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14935) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.14935v2) · [Source 3](https://github.com/MCG-NJU/VideoChat3).

</details>

<a id="16-internvideo3"></a>

### InternVideo3

InternVideo3 compresses multimodal attention states while retaining input tokens, pairing efficient long-context attention with closed-loop evidence collection, memory, and verification for video reasoning.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12195) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVideo/tree/main/InternVideo3)

**Authors:** Ziang Yan et al.  
**First public date:** 2026-06-10 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** attention architecture, long context, agentic system

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/16-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/16-paper.png" width="820" alt="InternVideo3: Author figure: architecture overview of InternVideo3." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 7, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12195). Author figure: architecture overview of InternVideo3.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A pretrained multimodal backbone is converted from grouped-query attention to Multimodal Multi-head Latent Attention, storing compact latent KV states and reconstructing head-specific keys and values during attention. Its visual-language token interface remains usable for video inputs. Multimodal Contextual Reasoning maintains observations, reasoning traces, tool actions, feedback, and memory in one evolving context for iterative answers.

**Temporal modeling.** The full multimodal token stream is retained as cached states are compressed. A video agent can revisit temporal evidence through retrieval and verification tools.

**Training / inference recipe.** Continue pretraining after attention conversion, then apply short-to-long supervised video tuning, rule-based reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks, and on-policy teacher distillation. The paper separately instantiates retrieval and verification tools around the trained backbone.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12195) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.12195v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVideo/tree/main/InternVideo3).

</details>

<a id="25-llava-onevision-2"></a>

### LLaVA-OneVision-2

Uses compressed video signals to allocate visual tokens around informative motion, joining codec canvases, sampled frames, and images in one perceptual architecture.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25979) · [Code](https://github.com/EvolvingLMMs-Lab/LLaVA-OneVision-2)

**Authors:** Xiang An et al.  
**First public date:** 2026-05-25 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, video tokenization, training recipe, dataset

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/25-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/25-paper.png" width="820" alt="LLaVA-OneVision-2: LLaVA-OneVision-2 architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.25979#S2.F2). LLaVA-OneVision-2 architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** The native OneVision-Encoder processes images, ordinary sampled frames, and compact codec canvases. Windowed attention limits local computation, while group visibility controls codec evidence interaction. A lightweight connector merges and projects visual embeddings into Qwen3-8B. Text and visual tokens share the autoregressive decoder; codec processing introduces no separate language branch or reconstruction decoder.

**Temporal modeling.** Packet bit-cost defines adaptive temporal groups; motion and residual cues select spatial patches. Shared 3D RoPE preserves source coordinates across codec and frame inputs.

**Training / inference recipe.** Four progressive stages move from image grounding and short captions to long video instructions and spatial supervision. The final stage mixes codec inputs with sampled videos and images, supporting both video grounding and spatial reasoning.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25979) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.25979).

</details>

<a id="34-minicpm-v-4-6"></a>

### MiniCPM-V 4.6

Targets mobile image and video understanding with a small language backbone and early visual compression, offering selectable token budgets within the visual encoder.

[Related encoding paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08985) · [Model](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-V)

**Authors:** OpenBMB / ModelBest  
**First public date:** 2026-05-11 (Official MiniCPM-V repository news: open-source release on 2026-05-11)  
**Contribution:** model release, visual encoding, token compression

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/34-schematic.svg"><img src="assets/architectures/34-schematic.svg" width="820" alt="MiniCPM-V 4.6: Visual tokens are compressed inside the encoder; mixed compression ratios control the budget." /></a></p>

*Editorial schematic based on [the primary source](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6). Follows the official model card. The bridge is a functional label, not a claim of a new named connector. The related LLaVA-UHD v4 figure is not used as the model's complete architecture.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** The official model card specifies SigLIP2-400M and Qwen3.5-0.8B. Its visual path adopts intra-ViT early compression derived from LLaVA-UHD v4 and supports mixed 4x or 16x token reduction before language decoding. The processor controls image slices and sampled video frames. This release differs from MiniCPM-V 4.5's explicit unified 3D-Resampler visual architecture.

**Temporal modeling.** Sampled video frames use the efficient visual path. Compression controls the spatial token budget; the model card's example specifies frame limits and stacking parameters.

**Training / inference recipe.** The release supplies instruction and thinking checkpoints and fine-tuning integrations. Its model card does not enumerate a complete pretraining corpus or staged video training recipe; the related visual-encoding paper describes a technique rather than this full checkpoint.

**Version note.** The official model card is the primary source for MiniCPM-V 4.6. LLaVA-UHD v4 is a related visual-compression method, not a standalone report with this model name.

**Temporal modeling.** Explicit timestamps and interleaved audiovisual inputs structure long contexts. Chunk-wise input processing supports streaming; ARIA aligns output speech with text and ongoing conversation.

**Training / inference recipe.** The report describes large-scale heterogeneous multimodal pretraining and staged Thinker/Talker post-training. Speech learning includes general and longer-context training plus alignment. Public documentation supports hosted inference; released model weights or a complete training implementation were not verified.

**Authors:** Junbo Cui et al.

<details>

DeepStack routes visual features from multiple encoder depths into corresponding decoder layers through residual connections, improving fusion without adding context tokens. Interleaved-MRoPE distributes positional dimensions across temporal and spatial axes, while video frames are accompanied by explicit timestamp text.

**Temporal modeling.** Textual timestamps directly anchor frames to video time. Interleaved-MRoPE balances temporal and spatial frequency allocation, complementing the frame sequence within long mixed contexts.

**Training / inference recipe.** Merger warm-up precedes full-parameter multimodal pretraining with progressively longer contexts. Video supervision includes timestamped dense captions and spatiotemporal grounding. Post-training combines supervised reasoning, teacher distillation, and reinforcement learning for stronger task execution.

<a id="51-streamingvlm"></a>

### StreamingVLM

StreamingVLM aligns short-chunk training with continuous inference, reusing bounded visual and textual KV windows to sustain coherent commentary over indefinitely long video streams.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09608) · [Code](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/streaming-vlm)

**Authors:** Ruyi Xu et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-10-10 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** streaming model, KV-cache policy, training recipe, benchmark

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/51-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/51-paper.png" width="820" alt="StreamingVLM: StreamingVLM inference: attention sinks, recent vision, longer text history, and bounded contiguous RoPE indices." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.09608v1/inference.png). StreamingVLM inference: attention sinks, recent vision, longer text history, and bounded contiguous RoPE indices.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A Qwen2.5-VL backbone processes interleaved video and text while retaining a compact KV cache. Attention sinks stabilize attention, a short recent-vision window captures ongoing actions, and a longer text window carries prior commentary. Evicted states are omitted rather than recomputed. Contiguous RoPE shifts indices into a bounded range so streaming positions remain close to training conditions.

**Temporal modeling.** Recent visual evidence and longer textual history provide different temporal horizons. Overlapping training chunks preserve context continuity and approximate the cache structure used in streaming inference.

**Training / inference recipe.** Fine-tune Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct on overlapped streaming commentary chunks with full attention. A subsequent annealing stage uses high-quality action commentary. The reported data combine Inf-Streams training samples and Live-WhisperX-526K; streaming behavior requires this SFT rather than cache changes alone.

**Data mentioned in the source:** Inf-Streams-Train, Live-WhisperX-526K.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09608).

</details>

**Training / inference recipe.** Encoder alignment precedes joint multimodal pretraining and longer-context training. AuT learns from speech recognition and audio-understanding data. Instruction tuning, distillation, and reinforcement learning refine outputs, with dedicated variants for reasoning and audio captioning.

### MiniCPM-V 4.5

Compresses images and adjacent video frames through one 3D-Resampler, pairing efficient visual tokens with unified document learning and short-versus-long reasoning post-training.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18154) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-V)

**Authors:** Tianyu Yu et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-09-16 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, token compression, training recipe

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/33-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/33-paper.png" width="820" alt="MiniCPM-V 4.5: MiniCPM-V 4.5 architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.18154#S1.F1). MiniCPM-V 4.5 architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** SigLIP2-400M encodes image slices and sampled video frames; Qwen3-8B supplies the language backbone. A unified 3D-Resampler uses learned queries to compress both modalities. Images use spatial resampling, while temporally packed frame groups are jointly resampled with spatial and temporal positions. Concatenated group representations form the compact visual input to the language decoder.

**Temporal modeling.** Adjacent frames share one resampling package with temporal query positions. Package size and sampling rate vary during training and can be adjusted during inference.

**Training / inference recipe.** Progressive pretraining first aligns the resampler, then adapts vision, then updates the full model. Dynamic visual corruption unifies document and OCR learning. Instruction tuning introduces the 3D-Resampler, followed by hybrid reinforcement learning for two reasoning modes.

### Flash-VStream (Flash Memory)

The later Flash-VStream replaces STAR Memory with Flash Memory, balancing compressed long-term context and selected high-resolution details for asynchronous streaming video interaction.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.23825) · [Code](https://github.com/IVGSZ/Flash-VStream/tree/main/Flash-VStream-Qwen)

**Authors:** Haoji Zhang et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-06-30 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** streaming model, memory architecture, asynchronous inference

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/48-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/48-paper.png" width="820" alt="Flash-VStream (Flash Memory): 2025 Flash-VStream: Context Synopsis Memory and Detail Augmentation Memory within a two-process streaming framework." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.23825v1/method_new5.png). 2025 Flash-VStream: Context Synopsis Memory and Detail Augmentation Memory within a two-process streaming framework.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** The Qwen2-VL-based frame handler continuously produces visual features and maintains a feature bank. Context Synopsis Memory clusters low-resolution features across frames to summarize history. Detail Augmentation Memory retrieves high-resolution features from informative frames. These memories are interleaved chronologically, then read by the independent question handler and passed through the merger projector to the LLM.

**Temporal modeling.** Context clusters estimate information density over time; detail selection concentrates high-resolution evidence on informative moments while preserving chronological memory organization for temporal reasoning.

**Training / inference recipe.** Initialize vision encoder, merger projector, and LLM from Qwen2-VL-7B. Freeze the vision encoder and apply LoRA to projector and LLM linear layers on a 9K LLaVA-Video subset. This is the 2025 Flash Memory paper and Qwen implementation.

**Data mentioned in the source:** LLaVA-Video subset.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.23825).

</details>

<a id="50-timechat-online"></a>

### TimeChat-Online

TimeChat-Online removes static temporal redundancy before language decoding, preserving original token positions and using video changes to trigger proactive responses during streaming interaction.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.17343) · [Code](https://github.com/yaolinli/TimeChat-Online)

**Authors:** Linli Yao et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-04-24 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** streaming model, token pruning, instruction data, proactive interaction

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/50-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/50-paper.png" width="820" alt="TimeChat-Online: Differential Token Drop: encode frames, compare adjacent patch tokens, drop redundancy, and retain original positions." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.17343v1/model.png). Differential Token Drop: encode frames, compare adjacent patch tokens, drop redundancy, and retain original positions.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** Qwen2.5-VL encodes densely sampled video frames. Differential Token Drop compares spatially corresponding tokens in consecutive frames and removes sufficiently similar features. The surviving tokens retain their original multimodal RoPE indices before entering the projector and language model. A FIFO bank stores recent compressed tokens, and low drop ratios identify scene changes that can trigger proactive responding.

**Temporal modeling.** Adjacent-frame differences retain changing content; preserving temporal, height, and width indices avoids positional distortion after pruning. Scene-oriented change signals determine proactive response times.

**Training / inference recipe.** Freeze the vision encoder and fine-tune the full projector and LLM on mixed offline and online instruction data. TimeChat-Online-139K includes timestamped streaming questions and unanswerable cases. DTD itself is nonparametric, but the complete online assistant receives supervised training.

**Data mentioned in the source:** TimeChat-Online-139K, LLaVA-Video-178K subsets, Tarsier2 subsets.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.17343).

</details>

### Slow-Fast Video MLLM

Keeps detailed visual evidence available through cross-attention while compressed preview tokens enter self-attention, allowing instruction-aware video reading inside a hybrid language decoder.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01328) · [Code](https://github.com/SHI-Labs/Slow-Fast-Video-Multimodal-LLM)

**Authors:** Min Shi et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-04-02 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, hybrid attention, query conditioning

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/64-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/64-paper.png" width="820" alt="Slow-Fast Video MLLM: Slow-Fast Video MLLM architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.01328#S1.F2). Slow-Fast Video MLLM architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** ConvNeXt-XXL and a projector form slow visual features. Strided sampling and temporal pooling create compressed fast tokens concatenated with text for Qwen2-7B self-attention. Selected decoder layers add cross-attention from text to uncompressed slow features. A dynamic gate and warm-up factor control this residual pathway, preserving detail without loading every visual token into self-attention.

**Temporal modeling.** Fast tokens give a broad temporal preview, while text-conditioned cross-attention reads detailed slow evidence. Temporal pooling controls preview length without discarding the accessible slow representation.

**Training / inference recipe.** Cross-attention projections inherit language self-attention weights where applicable, with a warm-up gate stabilizing integration. Visual-language alignment precedes mixed image, video, and text instruction tuning, teaching the hybrid decoder to select useful fine-grained evidence.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01328) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.01328).

### Qwen2.5-Omni

Separates multimodal reasoning from speech generation using Thinker and Talker, aligning audio and video in time while producing streaming text and spoken responses.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20215) · [Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen2.5-Omni)

**Authors:** Jin Xu et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-03-26 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** omni architecture, temporal alignment, streaming generation

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/60-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/60-paper.png" width="820" alt="Qwen2.5-Omni: Qwen2.5-Omni architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20215). Qwen2.5-Omni architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** Qwen2.5-VL vision and Qwen2-Audio-derived audio encoders feed the Thinker language decoder. Time-aligned Multimodal RoPE integrates audio timestamps and frame spatial positions. Thinker emits text and hidden representations to Talker, a speech-generation decoder sharing conversation context. Speech codec tokens are rendered through a streaming waveform decoder, yielding one end-to-end trainable multimodal system.

**Temporal modeling.** Block-wise audiovisual processing and TMRoPE place audio segments and video frames on a common time scale. Streaming generation begins before the complete response is available.

**Training / inference recipe.** Encoder and adapter alignment first freezes the language backbone. Joint multimodal pretraining then updates all components, followed by longer-context training. Supervised instruction tuning and preference optimization refine understanding, conversational behavior, and speech generation.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20215) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.20215).

</details>

<a id="30-qwen2-5-vl"></a>

### Qwen2.5-VL

Adds efficient windowed vision attention, dynamic video sampling, and absolute-time positions to the Qwen vision-language stack for long videos and precise temporal localization.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13923) · [Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen2.5-VL)

**Authors:** Shuai Bai et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-02-19 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, position encoding, training recipe

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/30-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/30-paper.png" width="820" alt="Qwen2.5-VL: Qwen2.5-VL architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13923). Qwen2.5-VL architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A dynamic-resolution ViT processes native-size images and video tubelets, using mostly window attention with selected global layers. Spatial merging maps visual features into the Qwen2.5 decoder. RMSNorm and SwiGLU align the vision architecture with the language backbone. The decoder consumes mixed text and visual tokens, with MRoPE time IDs tied to actual timestamps.

**Temporal modeling.** Dynamic FPS training exposes variable sampling rates. Absolute-time temporal IDs preserve elapsed-time meaning, helping the model distinguish event speed and localize moments.

**Training / inference recipe.** Progressive multimodal pretraining increases capability and sequence length using image, video, document, grounding, and text data. Supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization then improve instruction adherence and behavioral alignment across supported tasks.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13923) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13923).

</details>

<a id="13-videollama-3"></a>

### VideoLLaMA 3

VideoLLaMA 3 combines any-resolution vision tokenization with differential frame pruning, transferring strong image understanding into efficient video perception through a staged training curriculum.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13106) · [Code](https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/VideoLLaMA3)

**Authors:** Boqiang Zhang et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-01-22 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, token compression, training recipe

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/13-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/13-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoLLaMA 3: Author figure: architecture overview of VideoLLaMA 3." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13106). Author figure: architecture overview of VideoLLaMA 3.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A SigLIP-initialized vision transformer is adapted to variable resolution using 2D rotary positional embeddings. Differential Frame Pruning removes redundant patches by comparing adjacent frames in pixel space. Remaining visual features pass through a multimodal projector into a Qwen2.5 language backbone. Explicit textual timestamps distinguish video frames; the model supports image, offline video, and interleaved streaming inputs.

**Temporal modeling.** Adjacent-frame patch differences drive redundancy removal. Retained frame tokens and timestamps enter the LLM in order, concentrating the context budget on changing video evidence.

**Training / inference recipe.** The four stages are vision-encoder adaptation, vision-language alignment, multitask instruction fine-tuning, and video-centric fine-tuning. The first stage freezes the LLM; later stages train all parameters and introduce video compression and increasingly video-focused supervision.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13106) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13106v4) · [Source 3](https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/VideoLLaMA3).

</details>

### InternVideo2.5

InternVideo2.5 augments InternVL2.5 with hierarchical visual compression and task preference optimization, combining longer video context with richer supervision for fine-grained perception and reasoning.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12386) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVideo/tree/main/InternVideo2.5)

**Authors:** Yi Wang et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-01-21 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, token compression, preference optimization

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/15-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/15-paper.png" width="820" alt="InternVideo2.5: Author figure: architecture overview of InternVideo2.5." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.12386v3#S2.F2). Author figure: architecture overview of InternVideo2.5.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** The system builds on InternVL2.5. Hierarchical Token Compression merges semantically redundant spatiotemporal tokens within and between video segments before the language decoder. Task-specific visual perception heads interface with the backbone through learned task embeddings. Rich annotations and Task Preference Optimization jointly refine detailed localization, temporal perception, and the use of compressed long-range evidence.

**Temporal modeling.** Hierarchical compression exploits redundancy within and across temporal segments while preserving essential motion and events, increasing the duration that can fit into the language context.

**Training / inference recipe.** Use successive visual-text alignment, long-video context extension, and task-specific visual training stages. Rich vision annotations and Task Preference Optimization supply additional preference supervision for perception tasks beyond generic video captions and question answering.

**Data mentioned in the source:** LLaVA-Video-178K, ShareGPT4o, VideoChat2, InternVideo2, MovieChat.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12386) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.12386v3) · [Source 3](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVideo/tree/main/InternVideo2.5).

### Tarsier2

The 2025 Tarsier2 report improves a Qwen2-VL-based video model through expanded multitask pretraining, frame-event supervision, and automatic preference optimization for comprehensive video understanding.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.07888) · [Code](https://github.com/bytedance/tarsier)

**Authors:** Liping Yuan et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-01-14 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** training recipe, temporal supervision, preference optimization

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/20-schematic.svg"><img src="assets/architectures/20-schematic.svg" width="820" alt="Tarsier2: The report changes pretraining, frame-event supervision, SFT and DPO; it retains the base interface." /></a></p>

*Editorial schematic based on [the primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.07888). Shows the inherited Qwen2-VL video path. Training innovations are annotated; this is not a claim of a new Tarsier2 connector. Earlier project checkpoints with the same name may differ.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** The report initializes its 7B model from Qwen2-VL and retains that backbone’s visual tokenization and language interface. Video tokens are processed jointly with instructions for autoregressive text generation. The principal changes concern supervision and optimization rather than a newly introduced connector. This report version should be distinguished from earlier project checkpoints also named Tarsier2.

**Temporal modeling.** Fine-grained annotations associate individual event descriptions with supporting frame intervals, teaching temporal grounding and reducing omitted events. The inherited video token sequence carries visual evidence to the LLM.

**Training / inference recipe.** Pretrain on 40M public and newly collected samples, then perform two-stage SFT using temporally grounded and natural descriptions. Automatically constructed preference pairs support DPO with fine-grained event evaluation, refining factual and comprehensive video descriptions.

**Data mentioned in the source:** 40M pretraining mixture, 150K SFT video clips, Tarsier2 preference data.

**Version note.** This card describes the 2025 report initialized from Qwen2-VL, rather than an earlier differently configured project checkpoint.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.07888) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.07888v3) · [Source 3](https://github.com/bytedance/tarsier).

<a id="44-videochat-flash"></a>

### VideoChat-Flash

Compresses video tokens hierarchically before and inside language decoding, combining local spatiotemporal merging with inference-time visual dropout for efficient understanding of long frame sequences.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00574) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/VideoChat-Flash)

**Authors:** Xinhao Li et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-12-31 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, token compression, inference efficiency

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/44-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/44-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoChat-Flash: VideoChat-Flash architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00574). VideoChat-Flash architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** UMT-L encodes short multi-frame clips with spatiotemporal attention. Similar-token merging and an MLP connector compress each clip before its tokens enter Qwen2-7B. A second, video-level stage progressively drops visual tokens across language layers during inference. The hierarchy exploits both local frame redundancy and the decoder's changing need for broad versus detailed video evidence.

**Temporal modeling.** Clip-level attention and merging summarize neighboring frames. Shallow language layers retain broad coverage, while deeper layers increasingly concentrate on relevant moments through progressive token dropout.

**Training / inference recipe.** Visual pretraining and short-to-long instruction learning combine images, short clips, and longer video supervision. Training teaches the compressed clip interface; the video-level dropout stage is applied during inference, rather than being used as ordinary training-time token masking.

**Version note.** The v1 submission is 2024-12-31 even though the arXiv identifier begins with 2501.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00574) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.00574).

</details>

### Apollo

Apollo combines image and video encoders with Perceiver token resampling, deriving a practical video-language architecture from systematic studies of sampling, fusion, training, and data.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10360) · [Official project](https://apollo-lmms.github.io/) · [Model](https://huggingface.co/Apollo-LMMs)

**Authors:** Orr Zohar et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-12-13 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, design study, training recipe, benchmark

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/17-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/17-paper.png" width="820" alt="Apollo: Author figure: architecture overview of Apollo." /></a></p>

*Figure 8, PDF page 21, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10360). Author figure: architecture overview of Apollo.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** SigLIP-SO400M supplies spatial detail and InternVideo2 supplies video features. Encoder outputs are interpolated to compatible layouts, concatenated along channels, and compressed by a Perceiver Resampler to 32 tokens per frame. Clip timestamps and projected visual tokens are supplied to Qwen2.5 language backbones, released at 1.5B, 3B, and 7B model scales.

**Temporal modeling.** The video encoder captures local dynamics; frame-rate sampling and timestamped clip sequences expose progression to the LLM. The paper studies frames and tokens per second independently.

**Training / inference recipe.** Apply the paper’s three-stage gradual training schedule, first learning the connector and then adapting language and visual components. Mixed text, image, multi-image, and video supervision is used when the LLM is trainable.

**Availability.** Use the official project and Apollo-LMMs model pages. Third-party code mirrors are not treated as an author implementation.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10360) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10360v1) · [Source 3](https://apollo-lmms.github.io/) · [Source 4](https://huggingface.co/Apollo-LMMs).

</details>

<a id="49-streamchat-liu-et-al"></a>

### StreamChat (Liu et al.)

Liu et al.'s StreamChat updates visual context at every text decoding step, allowing generated answers to track changes occurring after a question arrives.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.08646) · [Official project](https://jihaonew.github.io/projects/streamchat.html)

**Authors:** Jihao Liu et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-12-11 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** streaming model, cross-attention, positional encoding, instruction data

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/49-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/49-paper.png" width="820" alt="StreamChat (Liu et al.): Liu et al.&#x27;s StreamChat: cross-attention and visual feedforward experts with linear gates inside the LLM." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.08646v1/arch.svg). Liu et al.'s StreamChat: cross-attention and visual feedforward experts with linear gates inside the LLM.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** SigLIP frame tokens are mapped by an MLP into Qwen2.5. Inserted cross-attention blocks use text queries and visual keys and values, while visual feedforward experts update visual representations between blocks. Linear gates stabilize the added branches. A separate thread continually updates a FIFO visual-token queue that the decoder reads for each newly generated token.

**Temporal modeling.** Parallel 3D-RoPE assigns concurrent visual and text tokens the same temporal coordinate. Causal timestamp masks prevent text from seeing future frames during training.

**Training / inference recipe.** Progressively align the adapter, then unfreeze visual components during multimodal pretraining. Full-parameter instruction tuning mixes existing image/video instructions with densely timestamped streaming instructions derived from Ego4D and Vript. This cross-attention model is distinct from Xiong et al.'s memory system.

**Availability.** The official project advertised code as forthcoming at the audit date; Xiong et al.'s similarly named repository is a different system.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.08646).

</details>

### InternVL2.5

Scales an established vision-language architecture through improved visual encoders, curated multimodal data, preference optimization, and inference recipes, including multi-frame video understanding.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05271) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVL)

**Authors:** Zhe Chen et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-12-06 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** training recipe, data curation, scaling

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/26-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/26-paper.png" width="820" alt="InternVL2.5: InternVL2.5 architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05271). InternVL2.5 architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** InternViT-300M or InternViT-6B encodes each image tile or sampled frame. Pixel unshuffle reduces spatial token count before a two-layer MLP maps features into an InternLM2.5 or Qwen2.5 language model. Video frames enter the decoder as ordered visual inputs. The central stack follows earlier InternVL versions; improvements concentrate on scaling and optimization.

**Temporal modeling.** Video training uses frame sequences with one tile per frame. Their ordering enters the language context, without a newly introduced dedicated temporal encoder.

**Training / inference recipe.** MLP warm-up precedes optional vision adaptation and full instruction tuning. Data filtering, progressive model scaling, loss reweighting, and mixed preference optimization improve learning; chain-of-thought inference and test-time scaling provide additional gains.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05271) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.05271).

<a id="42-longvu"></a>

### LongVU

Adapts temporal and spatial compression to the video and question, using complementary visual features to preserve useful evidence within a limited language context window.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17434) · [Code](https://github.com/Vision-CAIR/LongVU)

**Authors:** Xiaoqian Shen et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-10-22 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, token compression, query conditioning

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/42-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/42-paper.png" width="820" alt="LongVU: LongVU architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.17434#S3.F2). LongVU architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** DINOv2 and SigLIP supply complementary frame features. DINO similarity removes redundant frames before feature fusion. A cross-modal query selects frames whose spatial detail matters for the question, while others receive stronger spatial pooling. Additional cross-frame spatial reduction removes repeated patches. Projected tokens enter Qwen2 or a lightweight Llama3.2 decoder for video-language understanding.

**Temporal modeling.** Compression first operates across frames, then within frames, then across repeated spatial tokens. Query-aware allocation preserves relevant detail while ordered retained observations support temporal reasoning.

**Training / inference recipe.** Image-language alignment and tuning are combined using LLaVA-OneVision image data. Video training draws from public instruction datasets including VideoChat2-IT. The adaptive compressor is trained within the video-language system instead of relying solely on uniform frame sampling.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17434) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.17434).

</details>

<a id="57-trace"></a>

### TRACE

TRACE treats temporally grounded outputs as causal event sequences, explicitly combining timestamps, saliency scores, and descriptions to unify video grounding tasks within autoregressive generation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05643) · [Code](https://github.com/gyxxyg/TRACE)

**Authors:** Yongxin Guo et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-10-08 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** temporal model, structured decoding, training objective

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/57-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/57-paper.png" width="820" alt="TRACE: TRACE training pipeline with visual/time inputs and causal time-score-text event outputs." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05643v1/nero-overview.png). TRACE training pipeline with visual/time inputs and causal time-score-text event outputs.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** CLIP frame features undergo slot-based compression and are concatenated with timestamp tokens. Separate encoders and output heads represent time, score, and text. Initialized from VideoLLaMA2, the language backbone decodes structured events rather than plain timestamp strings: each event contains its boundaries, an optional relevance score, and a description. Earlier events condition subsequent generation through causal event modeling.

**Temporal modeling.** Frame timestamps anchor visual evidence, while causal event sequences capture dependencies among temporal boundaries, saliency, and event semantics across multiple grounded moments.

**Training / inference recipe.** First initialize vision compression and task-specific encoders and heads. Then fine-tune the language backbone and task modules while freezing the vision encoder. Mixed temporal-task supervision teaches structured event generation; optional downstream fine-tuning specializes the same architecture for grounding datasets.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05643) · [Source 2](https://github.com/gyxxyg/TRACE#model-zoo).

</details>

LLaVA-Video develops a data-driven video assistant by tuning an image-capable LLaVA backbone on synthetic detailed captions and QA, with efficient frame-token representations.

**Authors:** Yuanhan Zhang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-10-03 (arXiv v1 submission date)

### Oryx / 1.5

Handles images, videos, and multi-view scenes at requested resolutions and token budgets, combining native-resolution visual encoding with dynamically adjustable spatial compression before language decoding.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12961) · [Code](https://github.com/Oryx-mllm/Oryx)

**Authors:** Zuyan Liu et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-09-19 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, dynamic resolution, token compression, training recipe

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/35-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/35-paper.png" width="820" alt="Oryx / 1.5: Oryx / 1.5 architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.12961#S3.F2). Oryx / 1.5 architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** OryxViT encodes arbitrary-resolution visual inputs using variable-length attention and adaptive positions. A dynamic compressor pools features at selectable spatial ratios, attends back to preserve details, and uses a shared MLP to project into the language space. Flattened visual tokens join text in checkpoint-specific decoders: Qwen2-7B or Yi-1.5-34B for Oryx, and Qwen2.5-7B/32B for Oryx-1.5. The same stack handles still images, videos, and multi-view scenes.

**Temporal modeling.** Ordered video frames and adjustable spatial compression trade visual detail for temporal coverage. Long-video supervision teaches continuity; the encoder primarily supplies native-resolution frame representations.

**Training / inference recipe.** Image alignment and supervised tuning first train the visual-language bridge. Joint instruction tuning then mixes image, video, and spatially annotated multi-view data. Open-source video instructions and synthesized long-video questions support broad temporal coverage.

**Version note.** Oryx-1.5 was released on 2024-10-23 according to the official repository. The language backbone depends on the version and checkpoint size.

<a id="29-qwen2-vl"></a>

### Qwen2-VL

Unifies variable-resolution images and videos with tubelet encoding and multimodal rotary positions, explicitly separating temporal and spatial coordinates inside a general language model.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12191) · [Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen2-VL)

**Authors:** Peng Wang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-09-18 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, position encoding, dynamic resolution

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/29-schematic.svg"><img src="assets/architectures/29-schematic.svg" width="820" alt="Qwen2-VL: Two-frame temporal patches enter the ViT; M-RoPE encodes time, height and width." /></a></p>

*Editorial schematic based on [the primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12191). Shows the video encoder/merger/decoder path described in section 2. M-RoPE is a positional mechanism; the drawing omits individual attention blocks and training stages.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A dynamic-resolution Vision Transformer encodes images and video using two-frame 3D tubelet patching, treating images as duplicated frames. Adjacent spatial patches are merged and projected into a Qwen2 language decoder. The resulting variable-length visual sequences are mixed with text; M-RoPE supplies separate temporal, height, and width components for multimodal position encoding.

**Temporal modeling.** M-RoPE distinguishes frame time from spatial patch positions. Two-frame tubelets aggregate neighboring observations, while frame resolution adapts to a fixed video token budget.

**Training / inference recipe.** Training first develops the vision component with image-text data, then jointly updates all parameters using mixed multimodal and text corpora. Instruction tuning freezes the vision encoder and further adapts the language model for user-facing tasks.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12191) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.12191).

### LongVILA

Scales long-video understanding through context extension, long-video instruction training, and multimodal sequence parallelism, coordinating a conventional visual-language model with a distributed training system.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.10188) · [Code](https://github.com/NVlabs/VILA/tree/main/longvila)

**Authors:** Yukang Chen et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-08-19 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** context extension, training recipe, distributed system

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/43-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/43-paper.png" width="820" alt="LongVILA: LongVILA&#x27;s five-stage training pipeline; context extension and long-video tuning scale the VILA stack." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.10188#S1.F1). LongVILA's five-stage training pipeline; context extension and long-video tuning scale the VILA stack.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** LongVILA retains the VILA vision-encoder, multimodal-projector, and language-decoder stack, with Qwen2 backbones in its experiments. Frame tokens occupy an enlarged language context rather than a specialized fixed-size video resampler. Multi-Modal Sequence Parallelism shards long mixed sequences across devices and balances visual encoding with language attention, enabling training on substantially longer video inputs.

**Temporal modeling.** Ordered frame tokens are modeled directly by extended-context language attention. Long-video instruction data trains global narratives and detailed questions, while sequence parallelism handles training cost.

**Training / inference recipe.** Five stages cover multimodal alignment, pretraining, short instruction tuning, text-based context extension, and long-video supervised tuning. The final stage updates all model parameters using MM-SP and automatically annotated long videos with caption and question tasks.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.10188) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.10188).

</details>

<a id="58-vita-vita-1-5"></a>

### VITA / VITA-1.5

Introduces open video-image-text-audio interaction through modality adapters and a shared language backbone; VITA-1.5 subsequently integrates end-to-end speech generation with progressive multimodal training.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05211) · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.01957) · [Code](https://github.com/VITA-MLLM/VITA)

**Authors:** Chaoyou Fu et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-08-09 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** omni architecture, interaction system, training recipe

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/58-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/58-paper.png" width="820" alt="VITA / VITA-1.5: Architecture of original VITA; VITA-1.5 adds end-to-end speech output." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05211). Architecture of original VITA; VITA-1.5 adds end-to-end speech output.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** Original VITA connects InternViT visual tokens and an audio encoder to Mixtral through separate adapters, using modality-state tokens and two model instances for interaction control. VITA-1.5 keeps visual and audio input adapters but adds a speech-generation path driven directly by language embeddings, replacing the earlier external speech-synthesis pipeline and reducing reliance on cascaded modules.

**Temporal modeling.** Sampled video frames enter as ordered visual tokens. Audio interaction uses dedicated state and interruption handling; VITA-1.5 improves speech synchronization through direct embedding-conditioned generation.

**Training / inference recipe.** VITA stages language tuning, modality alignment, and multimodal instruction tuning. VITA-1.5 progressively develops vision-language understanding, audio input, and speech output using caption, question-answer, speech-transcription, and text-speech data while balancing modality conflicts.

**Version note.** The diagram is from the original VITA report. VITA-1.5 changes the speech-generation and progressive-training path as described in the linked 1.5 report.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05211) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.01957) · [Source 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.05211).

</details>

<a id="23-llava-onevision"></a>

### LLaVA-OneVision

LLaVA-OneVision unifies single-image, multi-image, and video understanding using SigLIP, a lightweight projector, and Qwen2, emphasizing task transfer through a staged multimodal curriculum.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03326) · [Code](https://github.com/LLaVA-VL/LLaVA-NeXT)

**Authors:** Bo Li et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-08-06 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** unified architecture, task transfer, training recipe

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/23-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/23-paper.png" width="820" alt="LLaVA-OneVision: Author figure: architecture overview of LLaVA-OneVision." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03326). Author figure: architecture overview of LLaVA-OneVision.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** SigLIP encodes visual inputs and a two-layer MLP maps grid features into Qwen2 token embeddings. Single images use flexible AnyRes layouts; multiple images and video frames use lower token budgets. For videos, spatial interpolation reduces each frame to 196 tokens before ordered concatenation. The same autoregressive language decoder handles all three visual scenarios.

**Temporal modeling.** Spatially downsampled frame tokens enter the LLM sequentially. Cross-scenario training transfers image and multi-image capabilities to temporal video tasks without a separate learned temporal connector.

**Training / inference recipe.** Train through language-image alignment, high-quality knowledge learning, and visual instruction tuning. The final stage first strengthens single-image instructions, then mixes single-image, multi-image, and video examples to encourage transfer across the three scenarios.

**Data mentioned in the source:** LLaVA-OneVision data mixture, LCS-558K.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03326) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.03326v3) · [Source 3](https://github.com/LLaVA-VL/LLaVA-NeXT).

</details>

<a id="19-tarsier"></a>

### Tarsier

Tarsier uses a simple framewise CLIP-to-LLM architecture, focusing its contribution on large-scale multitask training, human-annotated descriptions, and evaluation of detailed video generation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00634) · [Code](https://github.com/bytedance/tarsier)

**Authors:** Jiawei Wang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-06-30 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** training recipe, instruction data, evaluation

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/19-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/19-paper.png" width="820" alt="Tarsier: Author figure: architecture overview of Tarsier." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.00634v2#S3.F2). Author figure: architecture overview of Tarsier.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A frozen CLIP ViT encodes each sampled frame independently. A frozen MLP maps frame features to the language model’s token space, and an end-of-image token separates successive frames. The concatenated visual sequence enters an LLaVA-NeXT-initialized language model for autoregressive generation. The architecture delegates inter-frame relationships entirely to the LLM rather than introducing a separate temporal encoder.

**Temporal modeling.** Ordered frame tokens and end-of-image separators expose sequence structure to language-model attention. Training on captioning, recognition, localization, and QA teaches how frames relate over time.

**Training / inference recipe.** Conduct large-scale multitask pretraining followed by instruction tuning on moderate-scale human-annotated detailed descriptions. During the reported Tarsier training, the vision encoder and MLP stay frozen while the LLM learns with next-token prediction.

**Data mentioned in the source:** WebVid, Ego4D, Spoken Moments, Kinetics, Tarsier human-annotated instruction data.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00634) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.00634v2) · [Source 3](https://github.com/bytedance/tarsier).

</details>

<a id="41-longva"></a>

### LongVA

Transfers an extended language context into vision through image-only alignment, showing that long-video capacity can emerge without dedicated long-video supervision in the base model.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16852) · [Code](https://github.com/EvolvingLMMs-Lab/LongVA)

**Authors:** Peiyuan Zhang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-06-24 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** context extension, training recipe, language to vision transfer

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/41-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/41-paper.png" width="820" alt="LongVA: LongVA architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.16852v2/image/uniresv2.png). LongVA architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** LongVA first extends the Qwen2-7B language backbone. A LLaVA-style visual encoder and projector then align images with this decoder. UniRes treats image tiles and video frames through a consistent visual encoding scheme: training images provide multiple grids, and inference videos reuse those grids as ordered frames. Spatial pooling controls each frame's token count.

**Temporal modeling.** Long-context language attention aggregates ordered frame representations. UniRes minimizes the image-to-video encoding mismatch, allowing the language model's enlarged context to accept many video frames.

**Training / inference recipe.** Continued text pretraining extends context using long documents and adjusted RoPE. Visual alignment follows the LLaVA image-training recipe under a train-short, test-long protocol. Optional preference tuning improves answers, but base long-video transfer does not require video training.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16852) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.16852).

</details>

<a id="45-videollm-online"></a>

### VideoLLM-online

VideoLLM-online turns a conventional frame-to-language model into an online assistant through streaming dialogue objectives, timestamped supervision, and continuous cached inference.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11816) · [Code](https://github.com/showlab/videollm-online)

**Authors:** Joya Chen et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-06-17 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** streaming model, training objective, data format, inference pipeline

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/45-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/45-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoLLM-online: LIVE model and training: interleaved video frames, language tokens, and streaming EOS supervision." /></a></p>

*Figure 4, PDF page 6, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.11816v1/figure3.png). LIVE model and training: interleaved video frames, language tokens, and streaming EOS supervision.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** CLIP ViT-L independently encodes incoming frames. A compact CLS and optional pooled spatial representation passes through an MLP projector into Llama-2 or Llama-3. Frame and language tokens enter the decoder in chronological order. A parallel visual encoder buffers frames while the language decoder maintains a continuous KV cache, supporting responses during an ongoing stream.

**Temporal modeling.** LIVE predicts whether each incoming frame should trigger language or silence. Streaming EOS predictions supervise response timing without repeatedly appending redundant dialogue turns.

**Training / inference recipe.** Train the projector and LoRA-equipped LLM with autoregressive language loss plus streaming EOS loss. Ego4D narrations supply online supervision; offline temporal annotations are converted into timestamped question-response sequences. CLIP remains frozen in the reported training setup.

**Data mentioned in the source:** Ego4D Narration Stream, COIN Dialogue Stream.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11816).

</details>

<a id="18-videogpt"></a>

### VideoGPT+

VideoGPT+ combines complementary image and video encoders with segment-wise sampling and adaptive token pooling, preserving spatial detail and local dynamics for conversational video understanding.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09418) · [Code](https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/VideoGPT-plus)

**Authors:** Muhammad Maaz et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-06-13 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, instruction data, benchmark

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/18-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/18-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoGPT+: Author figure: architecture overview of VideoGPT+." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.09418v1#S3.F2). Author figure: architecture overview of VideoGPT+.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A CLIP image encoder captures detailed appearance, while an InternVideo2 video encoder captures motion within sampled segments. Separate MLP projectors map their features into language space. Adaptive spatial pooling controls token counts; projected image and video tokens are concatenated and passed with the question to a LoRA-adapted Phi-3-Mini-3.8B language model.

**Temporal modeling.** Segment-wise sampling preserves groups of neighboring frames for the video encoder rather than relying only on sparse independent frames. Fusion supplies local motion alongside frame-level detail.

**Training / inference recipe.** Pretrain the image and video adapters in two separate stages on CC595K while freezing both encoders and the LLM. Then jointly tune the adapters and language-model LoRA on VideoInstruct-100K, VideoChat2 data, and VCG+112K video instructions.

**Data mentioned in the source:** VideoInstruct-100K, VideoChat2, VCG+112K.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09418) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.09418v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/VideoGPT-plus).

</details>

<a id="47-flash-vstream-star-memory"></a>

### Flash-VStream (STAR Memory)

The original Flash-VStream combines asynchronous frame processing and question answering with STAR Memory, enabling online understanding without re-encoding the entire video history.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08085) · [Code](https://github.com/IVGSZ/Flash-VStream/tree/main/Flash-VStream-LLaVA)

**Authors:** Haoji Zhang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-06-12 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** streaming model, memory architecture, asynchronous inference

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/47-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/47-paper.png" width="820" alt="Flash-VStream (STAR Memory): 2024 Flash-VStream: independent frame and question handlers connected through STAR Memory." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.08085v1/overall_framework.png). 2024 Flash-VStream: independent frame and question handlers connected through STAR Memory.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A frame handler continuously encodes video and updates STAR Memory alongside a feature buffer. Its spatial, temporal, abstract, and retrieved memory components retain complementary evidence under a bounded budget. A question handler reads the latest memory, projects visual features, and invokes the LLM. The two processes run independently, allowing new frames to arrive during question answering.

**Temporal modeling.** Spatial memory preserves recent detail; weighted temporal clustering summarizes historical events, and semantic attention updates abstract history. Retrieved memory recovers detailed frames nearest to major temporal clusters.

**Training / inference recipe.** Use two stages: modality alignment trains semantic attention and the projector with frozen vision and language backbones; instruction tuning additionally updates the LLM. Training follows LLaMA-VID image/video caption and QA data. This STAR Memory version differs from the later Flash Memory model.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08085) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.08085v1#S3.SS2).

</details>

<a id="12-videollama-2-2-1"></a>

### VideoLLaMA 2 / 2.1

VideoLLaMA 2 replaces query-only video compression with a spatial-temporal convolution connector and adds a separately pretrained audio branch for joint audio-video understanding.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07476) · [Code](https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/VideoLLaMA2) · [Code](https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/VideoLLaMA2/tree/audio_visual)

**Authors:** Zesen Cheng et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-06-11 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, audio-video understanding

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/12-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/12-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoLLaMA 2 / 2.1: Author figure: VideoLLaMA 2 audiovisual architecture." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07476v3#S1.F1). Author figure: VideoLLaMA 2 audiovisual architecture.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** Framewise CLIP ViT-L/14 features enter an STC connector comprising spatial interaction blocks and strided 3D convolution for temporal/spatial aggregation. Its tokens feed an instruction-following LLM. The audio branch converts sound into spectrograms, uses BEATs, and applies a two-layer MLP. Reported language backbones include Mistral, Mixtral, and Qwen2; later checkpoints vary encoder/backbone configuration.

**Temporal modeling.** The STC connector learns local spatial interaction and cross-frame aggregation before the LLM. BEATs contributes temporal acoustic features, with cross-modal reasoning occurring in the language decoder.

**Training / inference recipe.** Pretrain visual and audio connectors separately with frozen encoders and LLMs, then perform modality-specific multitask tuning. A final joint audio-video stage integrates the branches with audiovisual instructions; backbone choices should be matched to the released checkpoint.

**Data mentioned in the source:** Panda-70M, VIDAL-10M, WebVid-10M, InternVid-10M, CC3M, DCI.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07476) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07476v3) · [Source 3](https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/VideoLLaMA2) · [Source 4](https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/VideoLLaMA2/tree/audio_visual).

</details>

<a id="46-videostreaming"></a>

### VideoStreaming

VideoStreaming separates reusable streaming video encoding from question answering, combining propagated clip memories with question-conditioned selection to represent long videos compactly.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16009)

**Authors:** Rui Qian et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-05-25 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** memory architecture, retrieval, training recipe

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/46-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/46-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoStreaming: VideoStreaming framework: memory-propagated clip encoding and adaptive memory selection for a downstream LLM." /></a></p>

*Figure 1(a), PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.16009v1/overview.png). VideoStreaming framework: memory-propagated clip encoding and adaptive memory selection for a downstream LLM.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** CLIP frame features are spatially merged and projected into a small Phi-2 language model. Learnable summarization tokens condense each clip while incorporating memory from previous clips. Historical clip representations are stored independently of questions. Adaptive Memory Selection retrieves relevant timestamps, and a second projector supplies selected memory tokens to Vicuna for question answering and reasoning.

**Temporal modeling.** Memory propagation carries earlier clip context into later representations. Question-conditioned memory selection restores details from relevant historical clips while preserving their temporal order.

**Training / inference recipe.** First align the single-clip projector and train the compact encoder on image and short-video tasks. Then jointly train streaming encoding, selection, and the answering LLM on long-video QA, using pseudo temporal labels to warm up selection before weak supervision.

**Availability.** No author-linked public implementation was verified in the initial audit.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16009).

</details>

<a id="56-vtg-llm"></a>

### VTG-LLM

VTG-LLM injects timestamp knowledge into visual inputs and textual outputs, combining explicit temporal embeddings with slot-based compression for video temporal grounding and related tasks.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13382) · [Code](https://github.com/gyxxyg/VTG-LLM)

**Authors:** Yongxin Guo et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-05-22 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** temporal model, temporal embeddings, token compression, instruction data

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/56-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/56-paper.png" width="820" alt="VTG-LLM: VTG-LLM: visual/Q-Former encoding, sequence-time embeddings, slot compression, and absolute-time output tokens." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.13382v1/vtg-lm-overview.png). VTG-LLM: visual/Q-Former encoding, sequence-time embeddings, slot compression, and absolute-time output tokens.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A fixed visual encoder and Q-Former extract frame tokens. Sequence-time embeddings add both frame order and absolute timestamps to the visual representation. Slot-based token compression maps the growing frame-token sequence to a fixed budget before the language decoder. Special absolute-time tokens encode timestamp characters in prompts and answers, providing a shared representation for video evidence and generated temporal boundaries.

**Temporal modeling.** Sequence-time embeddings distinguish chronological order from absolute time. Dedicated time tokens make generated timestamps explicit, while compression preserves useful information under a fixed token budget.

**Training / inference recipe.** Train with VTG-IT-120K time-aware instructions and a sampled Valley subset, covering temporal grounding, dense captioning, and highlight detection. Initialize pretrained visual-language components and tune the temporal modules and language adaptation according to the paper's instruction-training setup.

**Data mentioned in the source:** VTG-IT-120K, Valley subset.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13382).

</details>

### LLaVA-NeXT-Video

LLaVA-NeXT-Video transfers an image-trained visual-language architecture to multiple frames, then improves video understanding through instruction tuning, context extension, and direct preference optimization.

[Technical source](https://llava-vl.github.io/blog/2024-04-30-llava-next-video/) · [Code](https://github.com/LLaVA-VL/LLaVA-NeXT)

**Authors:** Yuanhan Zhang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-04-30 (official blog publication date)  
**Contribution:** image-to-video transfer, training recipe, preference optimization

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/22-project.png"><img src="assets/architectures/22-project.png" width="820" alt="LLaVA-NeXT-Video: Official blog illustration of the multi-frame representation used by LLaVA-NeXT." /></a></p>

Projected visual tokens form a sequence for the language decoder; spatial pooling controls video token growth. The official report compares zero-shot image-model transfer, video-supervised checkpoints, and a DPO-refined model, with linear positional scaling extending inference context.

**Training / inference recipe.** Begin with an image-only-trained LLaVA-NeXT checkpoint. Fine-tune on mixed image and video instruction data, then optionally apply DPO using AI feedback on video responses. The official technical source is the authors’ April 2024 blog.

<a id="10-pllava"></a>

### PLLaVA

PLLaVA adapts image-trained LLaVA to videos with parameter-free adaptive pooling, smoothing dominant visual features while retaining frame order for detailed video description.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16994) · [Code](https://github.com/magic-research/PLLaVA)

**Authors:** Lin Xu et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-04-25 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, parameter-free pooling

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/10-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/10-paper.png" width="820" alt="PLLaVA: Author figure: architecture overview of PLLaVA." /></a></p>

*Figure 6, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16994v2#S3.F6). Author figure: architecture overview of PLLaVA.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A pretrained CLIP ViT-L image encoder and multimodal projector encode the sampled video into a time-by-space feature grid. Adaptive average structure pooling reduces that grid before flattening and concatenation with text embeddings. A LLaVA-NeXT language decoder with trainable LoRA adapters produces responses. The pooling connector adds no parameters, while the projector and language adapters are trained.

**Temporal modeling.** Pooling can operate across time and space; the reported default preserves 16 frames and pools spatial grids to 12×12, leaving temporal reasoning to the LLM.

**Training / inference recipe.** Initialize from released LLaVA-NeXT image-model weights and tune the multimodal projector and LLM LoRA on video instructions. The paper studies data and model scaling, pooling choices, and post-optimization to improve dense descriptions and stability.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16994) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16994v2) · [Source 3](https://github.com/magic-research/PLLaVA).

</details>

<a id="39-ma-lmm"></a>

### MA-LMM

Augments a querying transformer with bounded visual and query memories, processing videos sequentially while preserving historical evidence for language-based long-term understanding and conversation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05726) · [Code](https://github.com/boheumd/MA-LMM)

**Authors:** Bo He et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-04-08 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** memory architecture, sequential processing

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/39-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/39-paper.png" width="820" alt="MA-LMM: MA-LMM architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.05726#S2.F2). MA-LMM architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A frozen visual encoder extracts each incoming frame's features. A trainable Q-Former maintains two memory banks: historical visual features and earlier query states. Its attention reads these banks alongside current observations, and a projection bridges queries to a frozen language model. The framework builds on InstructBLIP and supports Vicuna or Flan-T5 decoders.

**Temporal modeling.** Memory-bank compression merges similar historical entries at fixed capacity. Sequential updates carry visual and latent query information through time without concatenating every frame into the LLM.

**Training / inference recipe.** Pretrained image-language components provide initialization. Task-specific training updates the Q-Former and projection while preserving frozen backbones. Experiments cover video reasoning, question answering, captioning, and an off-the-shelf memory extension, illustrating transfer of the memory mechanism.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05726) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.05726).

</details>
