<a id="40-longvlm"></a>

### LongVLM

Combines compressed local video segments with global semantic features, preserving the order of short events while giving a language model an economical long-video representation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03384) · [Code](https://github.com/ziplab/LongVLM)

**Authors:** Yuetian Weng et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-04-04 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, token compression, global local representation

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/40-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/40-paper.png" width="820" alt="LongVLM: LongVLM architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.03384v3/architecture_v2.png). LongVLM architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** CLIP-ViT-L/14 extracts frame patch features and class tokens from multiple depths. Within each temporal segment, hierarchical token merging creates compact local features. Global class-token features summarize the wider video, and both representations are combined in temporal order. A linear projector maps the video representation into a frozen Vicuna-7B decoder initialized from LLaVA.

**Temporal modeling.** Segment representations preserve chronology while hierarchical merging removes local redundancy. Global semantic features add context spanning the complete clip to the language model's temporal interpretation.

**Training / inference recipe.** Training uses Video-ChatGPT video instructions to learn the linear visual-language projection. The pretrained CLIP encoder and Vicuna remain frozen. The lightweight tuning setup isolates the benefit of combining local aggregation with global semantic information.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03384) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.03384).

</details>

[Back to models](#models)

<a id="08-minigpt4-video"></a>

### MiniGPT4-Video

MiniGPT4-Video extends MiniGPT-v2 with chronologically interleaved frame and subtitle tokens, combining visual evidence and transcribed language within the language model’s context window.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03413) · [Code](https://github.com/Vision-CAIR/MiniGPT4-video)

**Authors:** Kirolos Ataallah et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-04-04 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, subtitle integration

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/08-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/08-paper.png" width="820" alt="MiniGPT4-Video: Author figure: architecture overview of MiniGPT4-Video." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.03413v1#S3.F2). Author figure: architecture overview of MiniGPT4-Video.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** Frozen EVA-CLIP encodes each frame. Groups of four adjacent patch tokens are concatenated and linearly projected into 64 language-space visual tokens per frame. Subtitle text is tokenized and placed after its corresponding frame. The resulting interleaved visual-text sequence and final question are processed by a Llama-2 or Mistral language backbone.

**Temporal modeling.** Temporal structure comes from ordered frame-subtitle interleaving. Subtitle alignment supplies corresponding spoken content, while visual compression accommodates more frames inside a finite context window.

**Training / inference recipe.** Apply three stages: image-caption alignment, large-scale video-caption pretraining on VideoDB/WebVid, and video-QA instruction tuning. Keep EVA-CLIP frozen while learning the linear projection and using LoRA to adapt the language model.

**Data mentioned in the source:** LAION, Conceptual Captions, SBU, VideoDB, WebVid, Video-ChatGPT.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03413) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.03413v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/Vision-CAIR/MiniGPT4-video).

</details>

<a id="09-st-llm"></a>

### ST-LLM

ST-LLM exposes spatial-temporal visual tokens directly to the language model, using dynamic masking and global-local inputs to balance temporal learning and efficiency.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.00308) · [Code](https://github.com/TencentARC/ST-LLM)

**Authors:** Ruyang Liu et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-03-30 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, temporal learning

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/09-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/09-paper.png" width="820" alt="ST-LLM: Author figure: architecture overview of ST-LLM." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.00308v1#S3.F3). Author figure: architecture overview of ST-LLM.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** An InstructBLIP-initialized visual encoder and Q-Former encode every frame into compact spatial tokens. A linear projection maps the full frame-token sequence to Vicuna-v1.1-7B. The language model learns inter-frame relationships directly. Dynamic masking reduces visual sequence cost during training; a global-local input module combines detailed local frames with broad video context at inference.

**Temporal modeling.** Temporal dependencies are learned inside LLM attention rather than collapsed by a video-level bottleneck. Masked/unmasked consistency learning and global-local features improve robustness across video lengths.

**Training / inference recipe.** Start from an image dialogue model and perform one-stage video instruction tuning. Freeze the visual encoder and Q-Former, fine-tune the language model, and combine autoregressive supervision with the proposed masking objective on diverse video instructions.

**Data mentioned in the source:** VideoInstruct-100K, VideoChat, WebVid, NExT-QA, CLEVRER, Kinetics-710, Something-Something-V2.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.00308) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.00308v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/TencentARC/ST-LLM).

</details>

<a id="14-internvideo2-mllm-branch"></a>

### InternVideo2 (MLLM branch)

InternVideo2’s dialogue branch connects a progressively pretrained video foundation encoder to an LLM, adding query compression and instruction tuning beyond the standalone representation model.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.15377) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVideo/tree/main/InternVideo2)

**Authors:** Yi Wang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-03-22 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** video encoder, MLLM integration, multimodal pretraining

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/14-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/14-paper.png" width="820" alt="InternVideo2 (MLLM branch): Author figure: InternVideo2 dialogue branch and three-stage training." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.15377v4#S2.F2). Author figure: InternVideo2 dialogue branch and three-stage training.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** InternVideo2’s large video transformer supplies spatiotemporal features learned through video-token reconstruction and multimodal contrastive training. The dialogue stage connects that encoder to a BLIP-style Q-Former and an open language model. High-definition post-training adds local video crops and a global resized view, while visual queries compress these features into language-compatible inputs for conversational generation.

**Temporal modeling.** The foundation encoder models multiple frames jointly. High-definition post-training combines global and local video views and increases input frames to improve fine temporal and spatial evidence.

**Training / inference recipe.** First learn video representations with unmasked-token reconstruction, then multimodal contrastive objectives. Stage three adds next-token prediction for dialogue. Additional high-definition instruction training updates the video encoder and Q-Former while adapting the LLM using LoRA.

**Data mentioned in the source:** K-Mash, InternVid, InternVid2, WebVid, LLaVA/video instruction mixture.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.15377) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.15377v4) · [Source 3](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVideo/tree/main/InternVideo2).

</details>

<a id="55-hawkeye"></a>

### HawkEye

HawkEye extends VideoChat2 through grounding-oriented instructions and recursive cropping, refining coarse temporal choices into precise video segments while retaining general video conversation abilities.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10228) · [Code](https://github.com/yellow-binary-tree/HawkEye)

**Authors:** Yueqian Wang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-03-15 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** temporal model, instruction data, recursive inference

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/55-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/55-paper.png" width="820" alt="HawkEye: HawkEye&#x27;s inherited VideoChat2 architecture, trainable components, and grounding instruction data." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 8, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.10228v1/training.png). HawkEye's inherited VideoChat2 architecture, trainable components, and grounding instruction data.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** HawkEye retains VideoChat2's visual encoder, Q-Former, query tokens, and language decoder. It formats grounding as four coarse temporal choices: beginning, middle, end, or throughout. At inference, recursive grounding crops the selected temporal region and asks again, progressively narrowing the segment. The resulting boundaries are mapped back to the original video's timestamps for user-facing output.

**Temporal modeling.** Coarse temporal categories avoid brittle direct timestamp generation. Recursive cropping repeatedly increases temporal resolution, and randomized training crops vary each query's relative position.

**Training / inference recipe.** Add InternVid-G temporal grounding and segment-caption instructions to VideoChat2 instruction data. Freeze the visual encoder, tune Q-Former and query tokens, and apply LoRA to the LLM. Random crops balance temporal categories and reduce shortcuts between query wording and answers.

**Data mentioned in the source:** InternVid-G, VideoChat2-IT.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10228).

</details>

<a id="54-momentor"></a>

### Momentor

Momentor adds a continuous temporal token space and grounded event-sequence training to support segment-level video comprehension, localization, and reasoning over multiple events.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11435) · [Code](https://github.com/DCDmllm/Momentor)

**Authors:** Long Qian et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-02-18 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** temporal model, temporal tokens, training objective, instruction data

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/54-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/54-paper.png" width="820" alt="Momentor: Momentor architecture and training, including the Temporal Perception Module and grounded event-sequence modeling." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.11435v1/Momentor_3.3.png). Momentor architecture and training, including the Temporal Perception Module and grounded event-sequence modeling.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** CLIP independently encodes sampled frames, and a linear projector aligns them with LLaMA. The Temporal Perception Module extends the vocabulary with temporal tokens and injects time into frame representations. Continuous interpolation represents timestamps between discrete tokens; neighboring token propagation regularizes their embeddings. The decoder generates temporal boundaries and language, allowing grounded descriptions and cross-segment instruction following through one interface.

**Temporal modeling.** Interpolated temporal embeddings reduce timestamp quantization error. Grounded Event-Sequence Modeling connects ordered event descriptions to boundaries, while neighboring-token updates encourage continuity of temporal representations.

**Training / inference recipe.** Use modality alignment, grounded event-sequence modeling, and instruction tuning on Moment-10M. The reported implementation freezes CLIP and the LLaMA-7B backbone, updating the projection layer and temporal module. Segment-level and cross-segment instructions teach finer temporal reasoning than video-level QA alone.

**Data mentioned in the source:** Moment-10M.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11435).

</details>

<a id="52-timechat"></a>

### TimeChat

TimeChat links frame content with explicit timestamps and produces variable-length video tokens, supporting temporal grounding, dense captioning, and highlight detection through natural-language instructions.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.02051) · [Code](https://github.com/RenShuhuai-Andy/TimeChat)

**Authors:** Shuhuai Ren et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-12-04 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** temporal model, Q-Former connector, instruction data

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/52-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/52-paper.png" width="820" alt="TimeChat: TimeChat: timestamp-aware frame encoding, sliding video Q-Former, and a language decoder." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.02051v1/arch.png). TimeChat: timestamp-aware frame encoding, sliding video Q-Former, and a language decoder.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A timestamp-aware frame encoder binds each frame's visual features to a timestamp description through an image Q-Former. A sliding video Q-Former aggregates these frame tokens within successive windows. Its variable-length output is projected into a LLaMA-2 decoder alongside the query and optional transcribed speech. The model then generates descriptions and timestamped temporal predictions as text.

**Temporal modeling.** Timestamp descriptions anchor frame-level evidence to absolute time, while the sliding Q-Former models local temporal relations and scales the token sequence with video duration.

**Training / inference recipe.** Initialize from pretrained visual-language components, then instruction-tune Q-Formers and projector with LoRA adaptation of the LLM. TimeIT provides time-aware supervision across multiple video tasks. Training uses language modeling on answers, enabling shared decoding for localization and description.

**Data mentioned in the source:** TimeIT.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.02051).

</details>

<a id="53-vtimellm"></a>

### VTimeLLM

VTimeLLM builds temporal boundary awareness primarily through staged supervision, adapting a simple visual encoder and projector to timestamped event understanding with a language decoder.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18445) · [Code](https://github.com/huangb23/VTimeLLM)

**Authors:** Bin Huang et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-11-30 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** temporal model, training curriculum, instruction data

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/53-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/53-paper.png" width="820" alt="VTimeLLM: VTimeLLM&#x27;s three stages: feature alignment, temporal boundary perception, and instruction tuning." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.18445v1/framework.png). VTimeLLM's three stages: feature alignment, temporal boundary perception, and instruction tuning.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A frozen CLIP frame encoder extracts a feature for each uniformly sampled frame, and a visual adapter maps the sequence into Vicuna's embedding space. Visual tokens and user questions enter the autoregressive LLM together. The architecture uses a lightweight connection; its central innovation is the boundary-aware training curriculum that teaches event descriptions and temporal intervals through textual answers.

**Temporal modeling.** One hundred sampled frames provide an ordered video representation. Single- and multi-turn temporal QA associate events with relative boundaries, enabling localization and dense captioning.

**Training / inference recipe.** Align the visual adapter with image-text pairs; train LLM LoRA modules on large-scale multi-event video data with boundary-aware QA; then instruction-tune on high-quality dialogues. The second stage freezes the aligned adapter, separating temporal learning from initial visual alignment.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18445).

</details>

<a id="38-llama-vid"></a>

### LLaMA-VID

Represents video frames with instruction-conditioned context and pooled content tokens, sharply reducing long-video input length while preserving question-relevant visual cues for language generation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17043) · [Code](https://github.com/JIA-Lab-research/LLaMA-VID)

**Authors:** Yanwei Li et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-11-28 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, query conditioning, token compression

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/38-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/38-paper.png" width="820" alt="LLaMA-VID: LLaMA-VID architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.17043#S2.F2). LLaMA-VID architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A visual encoder extracts frame patches, while a text decoder such as BERT or Q-Former forms instruction-conditioned queries. Context attention selects relevant visual evidence and projects it into a context token. Adaptive pooling supplies content tokens describing the frame. Both enter a Vicuna-family decoder; the two-token setting uses one token of each type per frame.

**Temporal modeling.** Frames remain temporally ordered after query-guided compression. The content-token budget is configurable, so the advertised two-token representation describes a particular setting rather than every input.

**Training / inference recipe.** Modality alignment learns context attention and projectors from image and video captions. Instruction tuning updates the multimodal interface and language model. Long-video tuning uses movie questions and subtitles to extend the system to hour-scale narratives.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17043) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.17043).

</details>

<a id="11-videochat2"></a>

### VideoChat2

VideoChat2 combines a temporally pretrained UMT visual encoder with instruction-aware query compression and progressive training, providing the strong model baseline introduced alongside MVBench.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17005) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/Ask-Anything/tree/main/video_chat2)

**Authors:** Kunchang Li et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-11-28 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, training recipe, benchmark

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/11-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/11-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoChat2: Author figure: architecture overview of VideoChat2." /></a></p>

*Figure 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.17005v4#S4.F4). Author figure: architecture overview of VideoChat2.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** UMT-L encodes video frames with spatiotemporal context. A Q-Former compresses extensive visual features using learned queries, with instruction conditioning guiding relevant evidence selection. Projected query tokens enter a Vicuna language backbone; LoRA adapts language generation. The architecture separates visual compression from language reasoning and is trained progressively rather than attaching an untrained projector directly.

**Temporal modeling.** The UMT video encoder provides temporal features before query compression. Task-diverse instructions teach perception, ordering, localization, and reasoning across changing visual events.

**Training / inference recipe.** Use three stages: align UMT-L and Q-Former, connect their representations to the LLM, and perform instruction tuning. Later stages adapt the visual encoder and Q-Former; language adaptation uses LoRA alongside a frozen backbone.

**Data mentioned in the source:** VideoChat2 instruction mixture: 2M samples from 34 sources.

<a id="06-video-llava"></a>

### Video-LLaVA

Video-LLaVA uses LanguageBind to align image and video representations before a shared projector, enabling one Vicuna model to converse about both visual modalities.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10122) · [Code](https://github.com/PKU-YuanGroup/Video-LLaVA)

**Authors:** Bin Lin et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-11-16 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, joint image-video training

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/06-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/06-paper.png" width="820" alt="Video-LLaVA: Author figure: architecture overview of Video-LLaVA." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.10122v3#S3.F2). Author figure: architecture overview of Video-LLaVA.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** LanguageBind image and video encoders extract features already aligned through a shared textual representation space. A shared two-layer MLP with GELU maps those features into Vicuna-7B-v1.5 embeddings. Projected visual tokens and tokenized instructions are concatenated for autoregressive generation, allowing the language model to learn from a unified visual representation rather than unrelated encoder spaces.

**Temporal modeling.** The LanguageBind video encoder supplies temporal features from eight uniformly sampled frames; the shared projector preserves their video-token sequence for the LLM.

**Training / inference recipe.** First train the projector with mixed image/video-caption batches while freezing the backbones. Then tune the projector and LLM jointly on LLaVA-1.5 image instructions and Video-ChatGPT video instructions; the visual encoders remain frozen.

**Data mentioned in the source:** LCS-558K, Valley WebVid subset, LLaVA-1.5-665K, VideoInstruct-100K.

</details>

<a id="07-chat-univi"></a>

### Chat-UniVi

Chat-UniVi uses dynamic token clustering and multiscale aggregation to compress images and videos into a unified visual sequence for a conversational language model.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.08046) · [Code](https://github.com/PKU-YuanGroup/Chat-UniVi)

**Authors:** Peng Jin et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-11-14 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, token compression

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/07-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/07-paper.png" width="820" alt="Chat-UniVi: Author figure: architecture overview of Chat-UniVi." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.08046v3#S1.F3). Author figure: architecture overview of Chat-UniVi.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** CLIP ViT-L/14 supplies patch tokens. Density-peak clustering with nearest neighbors merges spatially redundant tokens and groups frames into events. Within each event, visual tokens can span multiple frames. A three-step aggregation constructs complementary detail and semantic scales; their concatenation is linearly projected into Vicuna-v1.5-7B before processing the conversation and generating text.

**Temporal modeling.** Frame clustering defines event groups; token merging stays within an event, and the final visual tokens follow event order to preserve temporal relationships.

**Training / inference recipe.** Align only the projection with COCO and CC3M image captions while freezing vision and language backbones. Then jointly tune the projection and LLM on image, multiple-image, and video instructions from LLaVA, MIMIC-IT, and Video-ChatGPT.

**Data mentioned in the source:** COCO, CC3M-595K, LLaVA, MIMIC-IT, VideoInstruct-100K.

</details>

<a id="37-moviechat"></a>

### MovieChat

Converts dense frame tokens into short-term and long-term memories, enabling a video-language assistant to retain extended visual histories within manageable language input lengths.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16449) · [Code](https://github.com/wenhaochai/MovieChat)

**Authors:** Enxin Song et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-07-31 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** memory architecture, token compression, benchmark

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/37-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/37-paper.png" width="820" alt="MovieChat: MovieChat architecture and video processing." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.16449#S2.F2). MovieChat architecture and video processing.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** EVA-CLIP and a BLIP-2 image Q-Former produce frame representations in sliding windows. Dense tokens enter a short-term buffer and are consolidated into sparse long-term memory. A video Q-Former and linear projection map selected memory into a language model. Global and breakpoint modes choose representations for whole-video questions or a particular observed moment.

**Temporal modeling.** Similarity-based consolidation merges redundant neighboring memories while maintaining chronology. The hierarchy retains recent detail and compressed history, extending video coverage beyond ordinary frame concatenation.

**Training / inference recipe.** MovieChat reuses pretrained Video-LLaMA-derived visual-language components, with its report centered on memory-based processing. MovieChat-1K provides long-video evaluation with global and breakpoint questions. The memory hierarchy does not itself establish a new large-scale pretraining recipe.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16449) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.16449).

<a id="05-valley"></a>

### Valley

Valley augments CLIP frame encoding with temporal aggregation and a language projection, unifying image and video conversations through two-stage alignment and instruction tuning.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.07207) · [Code](https://github.com/RupertLuo/Valley)

**Authors:** Ruipu Luo et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-06-12 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, instruction data

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/05-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/05-paper.png" width="820" alt="Valley: Author figure: architecture overview of Valley." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, PDF page 2, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.07207v3#page=2). Author figure: architecture overview of Valley.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** CLIP ViT-L/14 extracts patch and global features from sampled frames. A temporal module combines corresponding spatial positions across frames, while frame-level global tokens retain complementary information. A projection maps the unified visual tokens into StableVicuna-13B’s embedding space. The paper compares average pooling, learned weighted pooling, and a transformer-based temporal aggregation variant.

**Temporal modeling.** The three temporal variants progressively add frame importance and temporal variation modeling; the transformer variant combines sequence-derived features with average-pooled spatial representations.

**Training / inference recipe.** First train the projection on CC3M image-caption data and Valley-702K video-caption pairs. Then jointly tune the projection and LLM with Valley-instruct-73K plus LLaVA and VideoChat instructions, while freezing the visual backbone.

<a id="03-video-chatgpt"></a>

### Video-ChatGPT

Video-ChatGPT turns CLIP frame features into spatial and temporal tokens, then learns a linear interface to a frozen Vicuna conversational language model.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05424) · [Code](https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/Video-ChatGPT)

**Authors:** Muhammad Maaz et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-06-08 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, instruction data, evaluation

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/03-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/03-paper.png" width="820" alt="Video-ChatGPT: Author figure: architecture overview of Video-ChatGPT." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.05424v2#S2.F1). Author figure: architecture overview of Video-ChatGPT.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 extracts a spatial token grid from every sampled frame. Averaging over time creates spatial tokens; averaging over spatial positions creates one temporal token per frame. These two representations are concatenated and mapped by a trainable linear projection into Vicuna-v1.1-7B, initialized from LLaVA, alongside the user instruction.

**Temporal modeling.** Separate spatial and temporal averages compress the video. The ordered per-frame temporal tokens retain sequence information for the language model without a learned video encoder.

**Training / inference recipe.** Use autoregressive answer prediction on VideoInstruct-100K, combining human-assisted and semi-automatic annotations. Only the linear projection is adapted; both the CLIP visual encoder and Vicuna language model remain frozen during video instruction tuning.

**Data mentioned in the source:** VideoInstruct-100K.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05424) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.05424v2) · [Source 3](https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/Video-ChatGPT).

</details>

<a id="04-video-llama"></a>

### Video-LLaMA

Video-LLaMA adds separate visual and audio query interfaces to a frozen language model, combining frame aggregation with ImageBind-based cross-modal alignment for video conversations.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02858) · [Code](https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/Video-LLaMA)

**Authors:** Hang Zhang et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-06-05 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, audio-video understanding

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/04-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/04-paper.png" width="820" alt="Video-LLaMA: Author figure: architecture overview of Video-LLaMA." /></a></p>

*Figure 1, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.02858v4#S1.F1). Author figure: architecture overview of Video-LLaMA.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** The visual branch uses a frozen image encoder and frame-level Q-Former, adds frame-position embeddings, then aggregates frames through a Video Q-Former and linear projection. The audio branch extracts ImageBind features from audio segments, applies positional embeddings and an Audio Q-Former, and projects its queries into the same frozen LLM input space.

**Temporal modeling.** Position embeddings distinguish sampled frames and audio segments. Separate query transformers aggregate each modality into a fixed-size sequence before their features enter the LLM.

**Training / inference recipe.** Train the visual interface on WebVid-2M and CC595K, then refine with MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, and VideoChat instructions. The audio interface uses visual-text supervision through ImageBind’s shared embedding space, rather than direct audio-text training.

**Data mentioned in the source:** WebVid-2M, CC595K, MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, VideoChat.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02858) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.02858v4) · [Source 3](https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/Video-LLaMA).

</details>

[Back to models](#models)

<a id="02-videochat"></a>

### VideoChat

VideoChat offers an end-to-end video-embedding interface and a parallel text-based pipeline, connecting video perception with conversational language generation through lightweight adaptation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.06355) · [Code](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/Ask-Anything)

**Authors:** KunChang Li et al.  
**First public date:** 2023-05-10 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, instruction data, system

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/02-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/02-paper.png" width="820" alt="VideoChat: Author figure: architecture overview of VideoChat." /></a></p>

*Figure 2(a), from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06355v2#S3.F2). Author figure: architecture overview of VideoChat.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** VideoChat-Embed augments a pretrained ViT-G image encoder with Global Multi-Head Relation Aggregator modules for temporal processing. A BLIP-2 Q-Former, additional learnable queries, and a linear projection create compact inputs for StableVicuna. VideoChat-Text instead converts action predictions, captions, dense descriptions, and subtitles into a structured textual prompt for an LLM.

**Temporal modeling.** The embedding branch learns temporal aggregation inside the visual encoder; the text branch serializes time-indexed perception results before the language model reasons over them.

**Training / inference recipe.** First align the video-language interface with large-scale image/video-caption data. Then tune temporal modules, extra queries, and projection on detailed video descriptions and conversations. Most pretrained parameters remain frozen throughout the lightweight two-stage recipe.

**Data mentioned in the source:** WebVid, VideoChat instruction data.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.06355) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06355v2) · [Source 3](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/Ask-Anything).

</details>

[Back to models](#models)

<a id="01-flamingo"></a>

### Flamingo

Flamingo connects frozen vision and language backbones through a Perceiver Resampler and gated cross-attention, enabling few-shot understanding of interleaved images, videos, and text.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.14198) · [Official project](https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/DeepMind.com/Blog/tackling-multiple-tasks-with-a-single-visual-language-model/flamingo.pdf)

**Authors:** Jean-Baptiste Alayrac et al.  
**First public date:** 2022-04-29 (arXiv v1 submission date)  
**Contribution:** architecture, multimodal pretraining, few-shot learning

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/01-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/01-paper.png" width="820" alt="Flamingo: Author figure: architecture overview of Flamingo." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.14198). Author figure: architecture overview of Flamingo.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A frozen NFNet-F6 encodes sampled frames into spatial features. Learned temporal embeddings precede a Perceiver Resampler, which produces 64 visual tokens per image or video. Newly trained gated cross-attention and feed-forward blocks are interleaved with frozen Chinchilla language-model layers. Text queries read the most recent preceding visual input, while language self-attention carries earlier context.

**Temporal modeling.** Frames are independently encoded at one frame per second; temporal embeddings and the Resampler aggregate their spatiotemporal grid before language generation.

**Training / inference recipe.** Train the Resampler and inserted cross-attention blocks with next-token prediction on interleaved webpages, image-caption pairs, and video-caption pairs. Vision and language backbones remain frozen; downstream few-shot evaluation supplies examples in the prompt.

**Data mentioned in the source:** M3W, ALIGN, LTIP, VTP.

**Availability.** The original Flamingo weights and implementation were not publicly released. Community reimplementations are not labeled as the authors' code.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.14198) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2204.14198v2) · [Source 3](https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/DeepMind.com/Blog/tackling-multiple-tasks-with-a-single-visual-language-model/flamingo.pdf).

</details>

[Back to models](#models)

## Methods and systems

These records describe cache retrieval, token reduction, grounding refinement, or an agent/memory system around an existing model. Their diagrams identify where the method acts.

<a id="68-streammeco"></a>

### StreamMeCo

StreamMeCo compresses an agent's long-term memory graph and prioritizes recent relevant evidence, reducing retrieval cost for streaming video understanding without changing the visual-language backbone.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09000) · [Code](https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/StreamMeCo)

**Authors:** Junxi Wang et al.  
**First public date:** 2026-04-10 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** agent memory method, graph compression, temporal retrieval

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/68-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/68-paper.png" width="820" alt="StreamMeCo: StreamMeCo: isolated-node sampling, connected-node pruning, and time-aware memory retrieval." /></a></p>

*Figure 3, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.09000v1/Figure3.png). StreamMeCo: isolated-node sampling, connected-node pruning, and time-aware memory retrieval.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** Applied to a memory-based video agent M3-Agent, StreamMeCo operates after perceptual evidence has entered a graph. Edge-free Minmax Sampling (EMsampling) compresses isolated nodes, while Edge-aware Weighting Pruning (EWpruning) removes less useful connected nodes using importance and similarity signals. Time-decay Memory Retrieval (TMR) reweights query matches with temporal decay. The retained and retrieved graph evidence then supports the host agent's language-model reasoning.

**Temporal modeling.** Timestamp-aware decay favors recent relevant memories during retrieval, while graph compression limits growing historical storage and preserves important entity-linked evidence from earlier observations.

**Training / inference recipe.** The proposed compression and retrieval procedures require no new model training. They operate on memory graphs produced by an existing agent, with sampling, pruning, and decay parameters selected in evaluation. The contribution belongs to the agent memory layer rather than a new video encoder.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09000) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.09000v1).

</details>

[Back to models](#models)

<a id="69-flashvid"></a>

### FlashVID

FlashVID compresses video tokens without training, combining attention-and-diversity selection with tree-based spatiotemporal merging to retain representative evidence under limited language-model input budgets.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08024) · [Code](https://github.com/Fanziyang-v/FlashVID)

**Authors:** Ziyang Fan et al.  
**First public date:** 2026-02-08 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** training-free method, token selection, spatiotemporal merging

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/69-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/69-paper.png" width="820" alt="FlashVID: FlashVID: attention/diversity token selection and tree-based spatiotemporal token merging before the language model." /></a></p>

*Figure 4, PDF page 5, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08024v1/method.png). FlashVID: attention/diversity token selection and tree-based spatiotemporal token merging before the language model.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A pretrained Video-LLM's visual encoder first produces frame tokens. Attention and Diversity-based Token Selection chooses informative, diverse representatives using calibrated attention and feature diversity. Tree-based Spatiotemporal Token Merging then groups redundant features through constrained redundancy trees spanning space and time. The compressed token sequence enters the original connector and LLM, allowing the unchanged backbone to process more frames within its token budget.

**Temporal modeling.** Merging considers cross-frame spatial changes instead of matching only identical positions. Tree depth and breadth constraints limit temporal span and preserve local video dynamics.

**Training / inference recipe.** No additional training is required. Selection and merging use existing visual features and attention signals while preserving pretrained weights. The paper evaluates the method with LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-Video, and Qwen2.5-VL, illustrating a reusable inference module rather than a new checkpoint.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08024).

</details>

[Back to models](#models)

<a id="65-rekv"></a>

### ReKV

ReKV is a training-free inference method that stores streaming video KV states outside GPU memory and retrieves relevant states when a question arrives.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00540) · [Code](https://github.com/Becomebright/ReKV)

**Authors:** Shangzhe Di et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-03-01 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** training-free method, KV-cache retrieval, streaming inference

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/65-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/65-paper.png" width="820" alt="ReKV: ReKV: sliding-window video encoding, offloaded KV retrieval, and cached-context answer generation." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.00540v1/framework.svg). ReKV: sliding-window video encoding, offloaded KV retrieval, and cached-context answer generation.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** A pretrained decoder-based Video-LLM encodes the stream once using sliding-window attention. Video KV states leaving the active window are offloaded to RAM or disk. A query selects relevant cached keys and values through cosine-similarity retrieval, accelerated by compressed representations. Retrieved states return to GPU memory and serve as context for autoregressive answer generation, avoiding repeated video encoding.

**Temporal modeling.** The sliding window captures local temporal context during encoding; indexed historical KV blocks retain evidence from earlier video regions for query-conditioned retrieval and reuse.

**Training / inference recipe.** No additional training is required. ReKV changes attention, cache storage, and retrieval during inference while reusing pretrained Video-LLM weights. Its experiments attach the method to existing video-capable backbones; it is a cache-management method rather than a separately trained model.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00540).

</details>

[Back to models](#models)

<a id="66-streamchat-xiong-et-al"></a>

### StreamChat (Xiong et al.)

Xiong et al.'s StreamChat is a training-free memory orchestration framework, combining hierarchical video evidence and dialogue history for streaming understanding and multi-round interaction.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13468) · [Code](https://github.com/hmxiong/StreamChat)

**Authors:** Haomiao Xiong et al.  
**First public date:** 2025-01-23 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** training-free system, hierarchical memory, retrieval, benchmark

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/66-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/66-paper.png" width="820" alt="StreamChat (Xiong et al.): Xiong et al.&#x27;s StreamChat: selective frame stacking, memory formation, and contextual summarization." /></a></p>

*Figure 4, PDF page 5, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13468v1/Canvas_1.png). Xiong et al.'s StreamChat: selective frame stacking, memory formation, and contextual summarization.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** Selective Frame Stacking encodes and buffers informative visual features. Memory Formation organizes them into recent short-term memory, a long-term memory tree, and a dialogue memory. Contextual Summarization retrieves question-relevant evidence and constructs context for an existing MLLM. Parallel scheduling separates frame processing from interaction, so the system can keep accumulating memory while answering user questions.

**Temporal modeling.** Short-term memory tracks ongoing events; hierarchical long-term memory compresses earlier video. Retrieved dialogue history supports continuity across multiple questions about different temporal regions.

**Training / inference recipe.** No additional training is required. The framework reuses pretrained visual-language models and embedding-based retrieval, introducing storage, compression, summarization, and scheduling around them. This memory system and StreamBench contribution are distinct from Liu et al.'s separately trained StreamChat cross-attention architecture.

**Data mentioned in the source:** StreamBench (evaluation).

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13468).

</details>

[Back to models](#models)

<a id="67-timerefine"></a>

### TimeRefine

TimeRefine improves existing temporal-grounding Video-LLMs by generating coarse boundaries followed by iterative offsets, supplemented with an auxiliary head that penalizes localization error.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09601) · [Code](https://github.com/SJTUwxz/TimeRefine_code)

**Authors:** Xizi Wang et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-12-12 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** plug-in training method, iterative decoding, auxiliary objective

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/67-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/67-paper.png" width="820" alt="TimeRefine: TimeRefine: iterative temporal predictions and offsets, with an auxiliary L1 regression head." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.09601v1/method2.png). TimeRefine: iterative temporal predictions and offsets, with an auxiliary L1 regression head.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** The method retains a host Video-LLM's visual encoder, connector, and language decoder, demonstrated with VTimeLLM and VTG-LLM. It reformats the decoder output as an initial temporal interval followed by refinement predictions and offsets. An auxiliary regression head supplements the next-token head during training. The last interval and offsets yield the final localized segment, adding temporal precision without replacing the host architecture.

**Temporal modeling.** Iterative residual offsets refine coarse predictions. The auxiliary L1 objective distinguishes near-miss boundaries from distant errors, which ordinary token classification does not directly express.

**Training / inference recipe.** This method requires training. Grounding QA targets are converted into refinement sequences using progressively decreasing timestamp noise; non-grounding targets remain unchanged. Apply the host model's original training data and settings while adding next-token and auxiliary regression supervision.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09601).

</details>

<a id="70-slowfast-llava"></a>

### SlowFast-LLaVA

SlowFast-LLaVA extends an image-trained LLaVA-NeXT model to video without fine-tuning, combining sparse detailed frames with dense spatially pooled frames under a fixed token budget.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15841) · [Code](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-slowfast-llava)

**Authors:** Mingze Xu et al.  
**First public date:** 2024-07-22 (arXiv v1 submission date (UTC))  
**Contribution:** training-free method, dual-rate input, spatial pooling

<p align="center"><a href="assets/architectures/70-paper.png"><img src="assets/architectures/70-paper.png" width="820" alt="SlowFast-LLaVA: SlowFast-LLaVA: sparse spatially detailed tokens and dense strongly pooled tokens feeding an unchanged image-trained model." /></a></p>

*Figure 2, PDF page 4, from [the original source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15841). SlowFast-LLaVA: sparse spatially detailed tokens and dense strongly pooled tokens feeding an unchanged image-trained model.*

<details>
<summary>Architecture, temporal modeling, and training</summary>

**Architecture.** The existing image encoder extracts features independently for uniformly sampled frames. A slow pathway keeps relatively few frames with detailed spatial tokens. A fast pathway retains many more frames but applies stronger spatial pooling. Their aggregated visual representations are provided to the unchanged LLaVA-NeXT connector and decoder with a video-oriented prompt, trading spatial detail against temporal coverage explicitly.

**Temporal modeling.** Dense fast-path frames capture changes between sparsely sampled slow-path frames. Temporal evidence comes from ordered multiframe inputs rather than a separately trained video encoder.

**Training / inference recipe.** No additional training is required. The method reuses image-trained LLaVA-NeXT weights and adjusts sampling, feature pooling, token aggregation, and prompting. It differs from the later trained Slow-Fast Video MLLM, whose decoder includes a separate cross-attention route.

**Primary evidence:** [Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15841).

</details>
